SELECTED_INDEX: 9
CONFIDENCE: 0.55
EXPLANATION: Strong Raman bands at 2880-2980 cm⁻¹ (aliphatic C–H stretches) and a prominent 1450 cm⁻¹ CH₂/CH₃ bending mode indicate a saturated aliphatic framework.  Alcoholic C–O stretches usually appear 920–1150 cm⁻¹; the experiment shows three bands at 919, 982 and 1028 cm⁻¹ that fit this region.  The cluster of medium bands at 760-820 cm⁻¹ (763, 771, 797, 814 cm⁻¹) is characteristic of C–O–C ring breathing/wagging modes of a saturated five-membered ether (tetrahydrofuran) system.  Among the candidates, only molecule 9 (OCC1CCCO1, tetrahydrofurfuryl alcohol) contains a tetrahydrofuran ring plus a primary alcohol, matching all these spectral features, whereas the other candidates are open-chain alcohols, amine, diazo, or different rings lacking the specific 5-membered ether signature.
